reason: Value/transfer lens: the realistic public gain is below +0.002 and cannot be seen through LB noise 0.003. (1) The metric arithmetic is right but it is not the constraint. Official aggregation: edge score = sum TP_i*pen_i / sum D_i. An added node costs 0.1*TP_i/T_true_i / sumD. On hold12 (exp02 validator_results.csv) break-even is 0.0004-0.0009 TP edges per added node on 44b6 and 0.002-0.016 on 6bba, about 5-9% real-nucleus precision. The binding constraint is REACH. (2) Reach of arm (a): fn_anatomy_exp39.md says only 424 of the 2,929 detection-side FN have their matched end on a free track end or start (+28 one-frame bridges). Swaps (2,175) have both ends linked elsewhere, so extension cannot touch them. a_tail (606) nodes still exist when byteext runs (before the short-track filter), inside the 2 um exclusion, so pool nodes cannot land there. The idea's 'directly reachable a_never+a_tail = 2,513 -> +0.0186' is therefore overstated about 5x for arm (a). On x138, readmit (>=0.965 within 4 um of open ends, 1,337 nodes = 1.1% on the dummy clips) and gapfill (0.5 peaks bridging end->start, <=3 frames) have already taken the easiest part of that 424. Estimate: 424 x chain ~2.5 x pool-hit 0.3-0.5 x not-yet-taken 0.5-0.7 = 150-370 FN->TP = +0.0011..+0.0027 local gross. Minus the node cost of extending genuine track ends (cells leaving, FP tracks, duplicates at 2-4 um): 0.5-2% nodes = -0.0005..-0.0018. Minus match steals and new FP. Net about 0..+0.0012 local. (3) Arm (b), births, is the only path to the swap oracle, but its gate (>4 um from nodes on 80% of frames) sits right at the swap geometry (GT 4.4/4.7 um median from our nodes, l6 report s.3). Whether pool peaks exist there is unmeasured. The loss normalises negatives per count (train_unet_transformer.py: w_neg = 0.1/n_neg), so unannotated nuclei are hardly suppressed (6bba N_pred/N_est 0.86-1.06), which weakens the premise that real nuclei hide in the 0.5-0.965 band. (4) Direct public-LB evidence on the SAME pool and the SAME public embryo (browser_research_2026-09-24.md l.118-121, 194): flow2 0.947 -> +gapfill(0.5 peaks) 0.947 -> +readmit 0.946, i.e. 0 and -0.001. Marginal-node populations are <= break-even on public: det threshold 0.965->0.95 gave 0.940 vs 0.941; MIN_TRACK_LEN 6->4 gave -0.002 (keeping 4-5 frame ILP tracks at >=0.965 hurts); zhincez min-len 10 gave +0.013 offline and -0.004 on the LB. Byteext adds exactly these kinds of objects (short extensions, low-score births). (5) The claim that the lab under-estimates is only half true. The out-of-sample detector also raises junk and duplicate peaks on test, and the one public measurement of pool usage is flat. Estimate: public central ~+0.0007 (range -0.001..+0.002), P(true gain >= +0.002) ~0.15-0.2. Even a true +0.002 is a coin flip to show on one probe at sd ~0.003. It costs ~5 GPU-h and 1 LB slot.
fix_if_any: Do not run it as a standalone GPU-lab + LB-probe line. Repair it into a cheap, gated rider. (i) STEP 0 only, CPU, from exp56's existing kernel output on the 4 dummy clips (edge_cache npz low_coords/low_score + submission.csv). Measure: (a) the share of FN-edge GT nodes with a FREE pool peak >= 0.5 at 2-4.5 um from any final node within 3 um of GT; (b) the distance histogram of free peaks to the nearest node (duplicates); (c) for every track end, the fraction whose byte extension lands within 3 um of an annotated GT node vs nowhere near GT. Kill if (a) < 15%, or if the extension hit rate at annotated nuclei is < 2x the video's annotation fraction (that means junk ends dominate). (ii) If it passes, keep only arm (a) restricted to ends whose last 3 steps agree with the flow prior (motion-consistent). Pass pool peaks through the V1284 head (the lowdet-refine rider) so added nodes are not left on the 1.625 um lattice. Keep the 3% guard, but cap at 1% on 6bba-like density. (iii) Put it as a rider in a multi-change probe with other small post-proc riders (lowdet-refine, divins), or use it only as F2 diversification. Never adopt on a single-probe delta < +0.003. (iv) Arm (b) births only if step 0 shows free pool peaks at >= 30% of swap GT nodes; otherwise drop it. If step 1 is needed, run it on friend A's x138 lab cache (CPU) instead of 5 new GPU-h.
realistic_public_gain: +0.0007 central (range -0.001..+0.002); P(true >= +0.002) ~0.15-0.2; not resolvable on one probe (LB sd ~0.003). Anchors: gapfill 0.000 and readmit -0.001 on the same public embryo with the same pool.
realistic_private_gain: +0.0005..+0.0015 (similar to public; no network-confidence channel, so no in-sample-trap collapse, but the node multiplier and junk extensions scale with density; a dense 44b6-like private embryo adds variance in both directions).
